Extend the notch vertically enough to affect section and make the void visible as a meaningful spatial gesture.
Deepen the cut to increase publicness and legibility at the verified access edge without fragmenting the mass.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact block in all views, so repair integrity is strong, but the visible mass is still too generic and sealed for the neighborhood_living brief. The verified access edge is not answered with a convincing public void; the notch exists but is too small and semantically weak to count as an active ground threshold. In plan and section, the form remains mostly a rectangular extrusion with a minor corner bite, so the program’s required active edge, public space, and upper hierarchy are under-expressed. It does not fully collapse into the wrong typology, but it also does not yet support a plausible mixed neighborhood building sequence. The form is therefore not program-fit hard pass. A stronger carved courtyard/notch or a more explicit ground seam at the access edge is needed while preserving the dominant compact mass.
